architectures.name: Single ReAct Agent (All Tools)
architectures.explanation: Prone to tool hallucination, lost-in-the-middle context pollution, and fails on planted prompt injections (obeying attacker instructions 38% of the time).

architectures.name: Prebuilt Supervisor (langgraph-supervisor)
architectures.explanation: Improves separation of roles, but supervisory routing overhead inflates token counts and introduces sequential coordination latency bottlenecks.

architectures.name: GigBid Hand-Built StateGraph (Shipped)
architectures.explanation: Parallel fan-out reduces latency by 2.5x compared to supervisor; dedicated Claim Verifier guarantees 0 ungrounded claims; hard policy guard catches 100% of scams and injections.

single_agent_subgroup_analysis.scenario: Low-complexity, single-skill jobs with clear requirements and verified clients
single_agent_subgroup_analysis.why_it_won: On 4 out of 50 tasks (simple bug fixes with 1 deliverable), the single ReAct agent completed the entire evaluation in a single tool call with 35% fewer tokens than the graph fan-out overhead.
single_agent_subgroup_analysis.why_not_shipped: ReAct agent failed catastrophically on adversarial scam posts (falling for free trial asks) and hallucinated past metrics in 68% of complex enterprise proposals.
